case_title: NETAJI ACHYUT SHINDE (PATIL) & ANR. v. THE STATE OF MAHARASHTRA
trial_court_outcome: A-2 convicted, A-1 and A-3 acquitted
high_court_outcome: Reversed acquittal of A-1 and A-3, affirmed conviction of A-2
offence_finally_established: Murder under IPC s.302 r/w s.34
neutral_facts: The prosecution case was that on 5 July 2011, at approximately 5:30 PM, the accused assaulted the deceased and inflicted serious injuries with a sword as well as by fists and kicks. The deceased succumbed to his injuries at the hospital around 7:15 PM. The FIR was registered at 11:45 PM based on a complaint from PW-1. The trial court convicted A-2 but acquitted A-1 and A-3, finding the evidence against them doubtful. The High Court reversed the acquittal of A-1 and A-3, affirming the conviction of A-2. The High Court noted that the eyewitnesses' consistent testimony showed the accused were part of the attack, played an active role in assaulting the deceased, and left the crime scene together. Material objects recovered from the site and the shop supported the eyewitness accounts. The trial court overlooked the common intention and focused on the FIR, leading to the acquittal of A-1 and A-3.
